title: In Psalms 143 In What Ways Does The Psalm Encourage Us To Seek Gods Guidance
paragraphs: Seeking God's Guidance in Psalm 143

Psalm 143 stands as one of the heartfelt prayers of David, often referred to as a "penitential psalm." This moving passage points believers toward seeking God's guidance in times of distress, confusion, or spiritual dryness. Let's explore how this psalm encourages us to look to God for direction and wisdom.
The Context of Psalm 143

David writes this psalm during a period of deep trouble, likely pursued by enemies or facing overwhelming circumstances. His response is not self-reliance but a turning to God in prayer. The psalm captures the desperation and faith of a heart that knows only God can truly guide and deliver.
Admitting Our Need and Trusting in God's Faithfulness
David begins by recognizing his own insufficiency and God's righteousness:
Hear my prayer, O Jehovah; give ear to my supplications: In thy faithfulness answer me, and in thy righteousness. - Psalms 143:1 ASV

This sets the stage for seeking guidance. Before asking for direction, David acknowledges God's character—His faithfulness and righteousness. True guidance begins with a humble recognition that God is trustworthy and we are dependent on Him.
Confession and Openness Before God
David does not hide his struggles:
For the enemy hath persecuted my soul; He hath smitten my life down to the ground: He hath made me to dwell in dark places, as those that have been long dead. - Psalms 143:3 ASV
By openly sharing his trouble, David models for us the importance of honesty in prayer. Seeking God's guidance starts with bringing our real circumstances and emotions before Him.
Remembering God’s Past Works
David chooses to remember and meditate on God’s faithfulness in the past:
I remember the days of old; I meditate on all thy doings; I muse on the work of thy hands. - Psalms 143:5 ASV
This practice builds faith and expectancy. Reflecting on God’s prior guidance and deliverance gives us confidence to seek His direction in the present.
Actively Seeking and Waiting Upon God
David’s posture is one of active seeking:
I spread forth my hands unto thee: My soul thirsteth after thee, as a weary land. - Psalms 143:6 ASV
This image of outstretched hands and thirst shows a longing for God’s presence and guidance. We are encouraged to come before God with open hearts, earnestly desiring His direction.
Direct Requests for Guidance
David specifically asks for God to show him the way:
Cause me to hear thy lovingkindness in the morning; For in thee do I trust: Cause me to know the way wherein I should walk; For I lift up my soul unto thee. - Psalms 143:8 ASV

He prays for God to reveal His will, trusting that God’s lovingkindness will guide him. Notice the connection between trust and receiving guidance—David’s faith is the foundation for asking God to direct his path.
Dependence on the Holy Spirit
David concludes with a plea for the Spirit’s leadership:
Teach me to do thy will; For thou art my God: Thy Spirit is good; Lead me in the land of uprightness. - Psalms 143:10 ASV
Here, the psalmist recognizes that true guidance comes from God’s Spirit. This points us forward to the New Testament promise that believers are led by the Holy Spirit (see Romans 8:14 ASV).
Christ-Centered Application

For those who trust in Christ, Psalm 143 finds its fulfillment in Jesus, who is the Good Shepherd (see John 10:27 ASV). He promises to guide His sheep and give them eternal life. As we seek God’s guidance, we do so through faith in Christ, relying on the Spirit to lead us in truth and righteousness.
Summary and Encouragement
Approach God humbly, trusting in His faithfulness.
Be honest about your struggles and needs.
Remember God’s past faithfulness to build your confidence.
Actively seek and wait upon God for guidance.
Pray specifically for God’s direction.
Rely on the Holy Spirit to lead you.
Psalm 143 teaches that God delights to guide those who earnestly seek Him, trust in His character, and depend on His Spirit.
